title: Project Management Module 1 — Exam Review Quiz
subtitle: Concepts, Processes, and Knowledge Areas

questions.question: What best defines a project in project management?
options: A routine business operation with no end date
A temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result
A scheduled task repeated on a fixed cycle
questions.explanation: A project is temporary and creates something unique.

questions.question: Which statement best describes project management?
options: Managing daily operations through standard procedures
Applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet requirements
questions.explanation: Project management applies knowledge and techniques to meet project requirements.

questions.question: What are the traditional Triple Constraint elements?
questions.explanation: The Triple Constraint is scope, schedule, and cost.

questions.question: How many Process Groups are defined in the PMBOK framework?
questions.explanation: PMBOK defines five Process Groups.

questions.question: Which Process Group formally authorizes a project or phase?
questions.explanation: Initiating includes formally authorizing the project or phase.

questions.question: What is the key output of the Develop Project Charter process?
questions.explanation: The Develop Project Charter process produces the project charter.

questions.question: Which document authorizes the project manager to use organizational resources?
questions.explanation: The project charter formally authorizes the project manager.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area coordinates all aspects of the project management plan?
questions.explanation: Integration Management coordinates and unifies project management activities.

questions.question: How many Knowledge Areas are defined in PMBOK 6th Edition?
questions.explanation: PMBOK 6th Edition defines 10 Knowledge Areas.

questions.question: What is a program?
options: A single large project with many tasks
A group of related projects managed in a coordinated way to obtain benefits
A software tool used for scheduling
A training course for project managers
questions.explanation: A program manages related projects together for benefits not available individually.

questions.question: What is a portfolio in project management?
options: A collection of documents for one project
A group of projects within one department
Projects, programs, subsidiary portfolios, and operations managed as a group to achieve strategic objectives
questions.explanation: A portfolio aligns selected work with strategic objectives.

questions.question: What is the project life cycle?
options: The series of phases from project start to completion
The lifespan of the project manager
The duration of the project budget
questions.explanation: The project life cycle describes the phases from initiation to closure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Process Group?
questions.explanation: Optimizing is not one of the five process groups.

questions.question: What does project scope refer to?
options: The work required to deliver the product, service, or result
questions.explanation: Scope defines what work is included and excluded.

questions.question: What is a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
options: A hierarchical decomposition of the total scope of work
questions.explanation: A WBS breaks total scope into manageable components.

questions.question: What is a work package?
options: The highest level of the WBS
The lowest level of the WBS where work is managed and controlled
questions.explanation: Work packages are the lowest level of WBS decomposition.

questions.question: What is scope creep?
options: The uncontrolled expansion of scope without corresponding changes to time, cost, or resources
The process of reducing scope at closure
questions.explanation: Scope creep is uncontrolled scope growth.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of scope management?
options: To ensure only approved work is included in the project
questions.explanation: Scope management controls what work is and is not included.

questions.question: What is the Critical Path Method used for?
options: Determining the longest sequence of dependent activities that sets minimum project duration
questions.explanation: CPM finds the longest dependent path that drives project duration.

questions.question: What is float, or slack, in scheduling?
options: The amount a task can be delayed without delaying the project finish date
The difference between planned and actual cost
questions.explanation: Float is available schedule delay time without affecting the finish date.

questions.question: What does total float measure?
options: Delay allowed without delaying the project finish date
Delay allowed without affecting the early start of any successor activity
questions.explanation: Total float measures delay without moving the project finish date.

questions.question: What is a milestone?
options: A task with the longest duration
A significant point or event in the project, typically with zero duration
questions.explanation: Milestones mark important events and usually have zero duration.

questions.question: What is resource leveling?
options: Adjusting the schedule when resources are over-allocated or unavailable
Using the same resources for all tasks
questions.explanation: Resource leveling adjusts timing to resolve resource constraints.

questions.question: What is fast tracking?
options: Reducing project scope to save time
Performing activities in parallel that were originally planned sequentially
Adding resources to critical path tasks
questions.explanation: Fast tracking overlaps activities to shorten duration.

questions.question: What is crashing?
options: Reducing scope to meet a deadline
Adding resources to critical path activities to shorten schedule, usually increasing cost
questions.explanation: Crashing shortens the schedule by adding resources at increased cost.

questions.question: Which scheduling technique often increases risk and rework?
questions.explanation: Fast tracking can increase risk because overlapping tasks may require rework.

questions.question: What is earned value management primarily used for?
options: Measuring project performance and progress against the baseline
questions.explanation: EVM integrates scope, schedule, and cost to measure performance.

questions.question: What does CPI measure?
questions.explanation: CPI measures cost efficiency as EV divided by AC.

questions.question: What does an SPI greater than 1 indicate?
options: The project is ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: SPI above 1 means more value has been earned than planned.

questions.question: Which formula defines CPI?
questions.explanation: CPI equals earned value divided by actual cost.

questions.question: Which formula defines SPI?
questions.explanation: SPI equals earned value divided by planned value.

questions.question: What is a risk register used for?
options: Documenting identified risks, analysis, and responses
questions.explanation: The risk register captures risk information and planned responses.

questions.question: Which response strategy shifts a negative risk impact to a third party?
questions.explanation: Transfer moves ownership of the response to another party.

questions.question: What is risk mitigation?
options: Eliminating risk entirely by changing the plan
Reducing the probability or impact of a risk to an acceptable level
Passing the risk to another party
questions.explanation: Mitigation reduces risk exposure rather than removing it completely.

questions.question: What is risk avoidance?
options: Reducing the impact of a risk
Changing the project plan to eliminate the threat entirely
Accepting the risk with no action
questions.explanation: Avoidance changes the plan so the threat no longer exists.

questions.question: What is risk acceptance?
options: Taking no action and acknowledging the risk may occur
Transferring the risk to a vendor
Reducing the impact of the risk
questions.explanation: Acceptance means the team decides to acknowledge the risk.

questions.question: What is a stakeholder?
options: Anyone who may affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves to be affected by the project
questions.explanation: Stakeholders include any party with an interest in the project outcome.

questions.question: What is the stakeholder register?
options: A list of project risks linked to stakeholders
A document containing information about identified stakeholders, including interests and influence
A log of all email messages
questions.explanation: The stakeholder register documents key stakeholder information.

questions.question: Which organizational structure gives the project manager the most authority?
questions.explanation: Projectized organizations give the project manager the highest authority.

questions.question: In a functional organization, who has primary authority over team members?
questions.explanation: Functional managers control the team members in functional organizations.

questions.question: In a weak matrix organization, the project manager typically has what level of authority?
options: Little to moderate authority, often acting as a coordinator
Full authority equal to the sponsor
questions.explanation: Weak matrix structures give the project manager limited authority.

questions.question: What is a PMO?
options: An organizational structure that standardizes project governance and supports resources, methodologies, tools, and techniques
A finance unit that audits project costs only
questions.explanation: A PMO standardizes governance and supports project practices.

questions.question: Which PMO type directly manages projects and has the most control?
questions.explanation: Directive PMOs take direct control and manage projects.

questions.question: What is a project baseline?
options: An approved version of scope, schedule, or cost used for comparison
questions.explanation: Baselines are approved references used for performance measurement.

questions.question: What is integrated change control?
options: Reviewing, approving, and controlling changes to deliverables and project documents
questions.explanation: Integrated change control manages change requests across the project.

questions.question: What does the project management plan do?
options: Defines how the project will be executed, monitored, controlled, and closed
questions.explanation: The project management plan integrates subsidiary plans and baselines.

questions.question: What is a scope baseline?
options: The approved version of scope documentation used as a basis for comparison
questions.explanation: The scope baseline is an approved reference for scope performance.

questions.question: Which item is part of the scope baseline?
options: Scope statement, WBS, and WBS dictionary
Risk register and lessons learned register
questions.explanation: The scope baseline consists of the scope statement, WBS, and WBS dictionary.

questions.question: What is analogous estimating?
options: Estimating from detailed work packages upward
Using values from a previous, similar project as the basis for estimation
Estimating only after the project ends
questions.explanation: Analogous estimating relies on historical data from similar projects.

questions.question: What is bottom-up estimating?
options: Estimating the whole project using a top-down assumption
Estimating lower-level components and rolling them up to the project total
Estimating based on one similar project
questions.explanation: Bottom-up estimating aggregates estimates from lower-level components.

questions.question: Which estimating method is generally the most accurate but time-consuming?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up estimating is detailed and usually the most accurate.

questions.question: What is the Communications Management Plan?
options: A list of all emails sent
A component of the project management plan describing how, when, and by whom information will be administered and disseminated
questions.explanation: It defines communication requirements and methods.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) or RACI chart?
options: Map activities or deliverables to team members and roles
questions.explanation: A RAM shows who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed.

questions.question: In RACI, who is accountable?
options: The person who owns the outcome and approves the result
questions.explanation: Accountable is the final owner of the task or deliverable.

questions.question: What is procurement management?
options: The processes needed to purchase or acquire products, services, or results from outside the project team
questions.explanation: Procurement management handles external purchases and acquisitions.

questions.question: What is a statement of work in procurement?
options: A narrative description of products, services, or results to be supplied by a vendor
questions.explanation: The SOW describes what the seller must provide.

questions.question: What is quality assurance focused on?
options: Auditing processes to ensure standards are followed
questions.explanation: QA is process-oriented and checks whether quality standards are used.

questions.question: What is quality control focused on?
questions.explanation: QC is product-oriented and checks deliverables for defects.

questions.question: What is a lessons learned register?
options: A project document used to record knowledge gained during the project for future improvement
A training checklist for new hires only
questions.explanation: Lessons learned are recorded to improve future project performance.

questions.question: Why is the lessons learned register important during closure?
options: It supports capturing and archiving project knowledge for future projects
It eliminates the need for formal acceptance
It is only used for budgeting
questions.explanation: Closure finalizes lessons learned for organizational learning.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Closing Process Group?
options: To formally complete or close the project or phase and archive records
questions.explanation: Closing ensures formal completion and documentation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common output of project closure?
questions.explanation: Closure includes final acceptance and archiving of records.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a baseline change?
options: It can be made informally by any team member
It should be changed only through formal change control
It never changes under any circumstance
It is not used for performance measurement
questions.explanation: Baselines are controlled through formal change procedures.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a milestone schedule?
options: A schedule highlighting major zero-duration events
questions.explanation: Milestone schedules focus on key events in the project.

questions.question: What is the relationship between scope, schedule, and cost in the Triple Constraint?
options: Changing one typically affects the others
Only cost affects the other two
questions.explanation: The triple constraint elements are interdependent.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a project charter?
options: To formally authorize the project and define high-level information
questions.explanation: The charter gives authorization and high-level direction.

questions.question: Which item is typically included in a project charter?
options: High-level requirements and project manager authority
questions.explanation: The charter includes high-level requirements and authority details.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the project management plan during execution?
options: To provide the authorized baseline and guide project work
questions.explanation: The plan guides execution and control against baselines.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a project as opposed to an operation?
questions.explanation: Projects are temporary and unique; operations are ongoing and repetitive.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate use of a PMBOK guide?
options: To provide standard terminology and guidelines for project management
To serve as a legal contract
questions.explanation: PMBOK is a standards guide, not a contract or guarantee.
